CDB is a fixed-income security issued by banks: you lend money to the bank and earn interest, with FGC protection up to the covered limit.
Tesouro Direto is a government bond program: you lend money to the government, with options linked to the Selic rate, inflation (IPCA) or fixed rates.
LCI and LCA are fixed-income securities issued by banks and linked to real estate and agribusiness, exempt from income tax for individuals and backed by the FGC guarantee.
Savings are simple and you can withdraw anytime, but they usually earn less than other fixed income options.
Real estate funds (REITs) pool properties or sector securities and pay out income, but their shares rise and fall on the exchange.
Stocks are parts of companies traded on the exchange. They may pay dividends, but prices swing a lot, so they suit long horizons.
Private pensions (PGBL or VGBL) are made for the long term, with their own tax and withdrawal rules.
Cryptocurrencies swing a lot and have no guarantees like the FGC.
Investment funds pool money from many people under a professional's management, with fees and risks that vary from fund to fund.
Investing abroad (ETFs, BDRs or dollars) diversifies the portfolio, but brings currency risk.
